chunks: Then it is said to them: Did not the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) hide in the valley for three years, so that no one could reach him, and did he not hide in the Cave for three days? And by analogy, is it not valid that Allah should not deprive him of existence for that period, while the obligation remains upon the people for whom He sent him as a mercy?

If they say: He only hid after he called people to himself and manifested his Prophethood, and when they threatened him, he concealed himself. We say: Likewise, the Imam did not go into hiding until his forefathers had manifested his position and description, and pointed him out. Then, when his father Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) feared for him, he hid him and concealed him. Therefore, the two matters are equal.

Then it is said to them: Inform me, if Allah knew from the condition of a person that it is in his interest that Allah sends a specific prophet to him to convey his affairs, and He knew that if He sent him, this person would kill him, and if He prevented him from killing him by force, there would be a detriment to him or to others, would it be fitting that Allah obligate this person and not send that prophet to him, or not obligate him?
ai.seo_question: How does the hiding of the Prophet Muhammad justify the hiding of the Imam in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs this dialectical argument to refute the notion that the Imam's occultation (ghayba) invalidates his spiritual authority, drawing a parallel between the Prophet’s strategic concealment and the Imam’s divinely ordained hiding. He posits that just as the Prophet’s temporary absence did not suspend religious obligation, the Imam’s concealment preserves the necessity of his existence (hujjiyya) for guiding the community. The analogy of a specific individual potentially killing a prophet illustrates how divine wisdom balances the preservation of the leader against the potential harm to the community, affirming that the Imam remains the essential link to divine knowledge even when hidden.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Moreover, the opponents are asked: Did not the Messenger of Allah (s) hide in Sheb Abu Talib for three years, where no one was able to reach him? Did he not hide in the Cave for three days? Why don’t you apply the analogy there as well that Allah should discontinue his existence for that period, while keeping the duties over public for whom He sent him as a grace?

If they say that he hid after he called the people to his message and manifested his Prophethood, and when they threatened him, he went into hiding. We will respond that likewise the Imam did not go into hiding, but after his forefathers manifested his position and qualities and guided the people to him, and when his father Hasan Ibne Ali (a.s) feared for his life, he hid him. Therefore, both situations are identical.

To clarify the matter further, we tell them: Allah discerns from the condition of a person that it is in the best of his interest that He sends a particular prophet to him who will inform him of what is good for him, and He knows that should He send the said apostle, this person will kill him. If He prohibits him from killing the apostle through force, would it not be disadvantageous for him and others?
